summary.text: Comrade and charioteer of Meriones from well-built Lyctus, whom Hector smote when he cast at Idomeneus — distinct from Coeranus the Lycian whom Odysseus slew beside Scamander.

story.text: Idomeneus had come on foot from the curved ships and would have yielded great victory to the Trojans, had not Coeranus speedily driven up the swift horses; yet Hector cast at Deucalion's son and missed him by but little, and smote Coeranus the charioteer who followed Meriones from Lyctus.
